flow.name: flowchart
flow.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  flow "Title" {              open a flowchart; close it with }

Nodes
  start ID "Label"            terminator (ellipse)
  process ID "Label"          process step; alias: task
  decision ID "Label"         branch point (diamond)
  io ID "Label"               input / output; alias: data
  end ID "Label"              terminator (ellipse)

Edges
  A -> B                      directed edge
  A [Yes] -> B                edge with a caption
  A -> B -> C                 chain
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `flow "Title" { ... }` block. Nothing may sit outside it.
- An element is `<keyword> <ID> "Label"`, one per line. The ID is short, unique, and never quoted.
- Every ID used in an arrow must be declared above it.
- A decision usually has two outgoing arrows, each with its own caption: `D1 [Yes] -> E1`.

WORKED EXAMPLE
flow "Chart Title" {
  start S1 "Start Process"
  io I1 "Read Input Data"
  process P1 "Execute Algorithm"
  decision D1 "Is Valid?"
  end E1 "Finish"

  S1 -> I1 -> P1 -> D1
  D1 [Yes] -> E1
  D1 [No] -> P1
}

bpmn.name: BPMN 2.0 diagram
bpmn.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  bpmn "Title" {              open a BPMN 2.0 diagram
  pool ID "Label" {           participant, holds lanes
  lane ID "Label" {           role inside a pool

Events
  start ID "Label"            start event (thin circle)
  msg-start ID "Label"        message start (open envelope)
  timer ID "Label"            timer event (clock)
  end ID "Label"              end event (thick circle)
  msg-end ID "Label"          message end (filled envelope)

Activities
  task ID "Label"             task (rounded rectangle)
  send-task ID "Label"        send task
  recv-task ID "Label"        receive task
  script-task ID "Label"      script task
  user-task ID "Label"        user task

Gateways and data
  gw-ex ID "Label"            exclusive gateway (X)
  gw-para ID "Label"          parallel gateway (+)
  gw-inc ID "Label"           inclusive gateway (O)
  data ID "Label"             data object (document)

Flows
  A -> B                      sequence flow
  A [Yes] -> B                conditional flow
  A -.-> D                    data association (dotted)

RULES
- The file is one `bpmn "Title" { ... }` block.
- Participants are `pool ID "Label" { ... }`; inside a pool, roles are `lane ID "Label" { ... }`; elements are declared inside a lane.
- An element is `<keyword> <ID> "Label"`, one per line, and its ID must be unique across the whole diagram.
- Flows are declared after the pool block, at the top level, and may cross lanes.
- A data object is joined with a dotted association `A -.-> D1`, never with a sequence flow.

WORKED EXAMPLE
bpmn "Vacation Request" {
  pool P1 "Request" {
    lane L1 "Employee" {
      start S1 "Submit request"
      task A1 "Fill vacation form"
      send-task A2 "Send to manager"
    }
    lane L2 "Manager" {
      gw-ex G1 "Approved?"
      end E1 "Done"
    }
    lane L3 "HR" {
      send-task A3 "Record leave"
      data D1 "Request log"
      end E2 "Archived"
    }
  }

  S1 -> A1 -> A2 -> G1
  G1 [Yes] -> A3 -> E2
  G1 [No] -> E1
  A3 -.-> D1
}

org.name: organisational chart
org.briefing:
SYNTAX
Chart
  org "Title" {               open an org chart

Boxes
  role ID "Role" "Name"       role band over a name
  role ID "Role"              role band on its own
  role ID "Role" {            role band over sub-roles
  unit "Sub-role" "Name"      one sub-role, inside a role block

Lines
  A -> B                      B reports to A
  A -> B -> C                 chain of reporting lines
  A -.-> B                    advisory tie (dashed)
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `org "Title" { ... }` block.
- A box is `role ID "ROLE" "Name"`. Drop the second caption for a role with no name attached.
- A box that lists sub-roles opens a block: `role ID "ROLE" { unit "Sub-role" "Name" ... }`. `unit` is only legal inside such a block.
- `A -> B` means B reports to A. Use it once per reporting line.
- `A -.-> B` is an advisory tie, drawn dashed and left out of the reporting bus.

WORKED EXAMPLE
org "FACULTY OF PSYCHOLOGY ORGANISATIONAL CHART" {
  role DEAN "DEAN" "Dr. Marion Hale"
  role SENATE "FACULTY SENATE"

  role VD1 "VICE DEAN I" "Priya Raman, Ph.D"
  role VD2 "VICE DEAN II" "Dr. Elena Sorbo, M.Ed"
  role VD3 "VICE DEAN III" "Tomas Weller, Ph.D"

  role LABS "HEAD OF LABORATORIES" {
    unit "Psychodiagnostics Lab" "Ines Fabri, M.Sc"
    unit "Computing Lab" "Karel Sandvik, M.Sc"
    unit "Experimental and Media Lab" "Ada Moreau, M.Sc"
  }
  role UG "HEAD OF UNDERGRADUATE PROGRAMME" "Nadia Brenner, M.Sc"
  role PG "HEAD OF MASTER PROGRAMME" "Dr. Owen Castellan"
  role QA "QUALITY ASSURANCE CHAIR" "Sofia Lindqvist, M.Sc"

  role SERVICES "SERVICES COORDINATOR" "Rafael Duarte, M.A"
  role QA1 "QA TEAM, UNDERGRADUATE" "Hana Oyelaan, M.Sc"
  role QA2 "QA TEAM, MASTER" "Iris Kovak, M.Sc"

  DEAN -> VD1
  DEAN -> VD2
  DEAN -> VD3
  DEAN -> LABS
  DEAN -> UG
  DEAN -> PG
  DEAN -> QA
  UG -> SERVICES
  QA -> QA1
  QA -> QA2
  DEAN -.-> SENATE
}

usecase.name: UML use case diagram
usecase.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  usecase "Title" {           open a use case diagram
  system S "Name" {           the boundary the use cases stand in

Elements
  actor A "Name"              a stick figure outside the system
  actor A "Name" right        pin it to that side of the boundary
  usecase U "Goal"            an oval, declared inside a system block

Relations
  A -> U                      association: A takes part in U
  include U -> V              U always runs V
  extend V -> U               V adds to U, under a condition
  inherit A -> B              A is a kind of B (hollow head)
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `usecase "Title" { ... }` block.
- Actors are declared at the top level; use cases go inside `system S "Name" { ... }`.
- `A -> U` is an association and is the only relation written with a bare arrow.
- `include`, `extend` and `inherit` each take one relation: `include U -> V`.
- An actor with no side written takes the left if it starts anything, the right otherwise.

WORKED EXAMPLE
usecase "Bank ATM" {
  actor CUST "Customer"
  actor TECH "ATM Technician"
  actor BANK "Bank" right

  system ATM "Bank ATM" {
    usecase U1 "Check Balances"
    usecase U2 "Deposit Funds"
    usecase U3 "Withdraw Cash"
    usecase U4 "Transfer Funds"
    usecase U5 "Maintenance"
    usecase U6 "Repair"
  }

  CUST -> U1
  CUST -> U2
  CUST -> U3
  CUST -> U4
  TECH -> U5
  TECH -> U6

  U1 -> BANK
  U2 -> BANK
  U3 -> BANK
  U4 -> BANK
  U5 -> BANK
  U6 -> BANK

  include U3 -> U1
}

activity.name: UML activity diagram
activity.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  activity "Title" {          open an activity diagram
  lane L "Name" {             a partition; it is drawn as a column

Nodes
  initial S1                  the filled dot it starts at; alias: start
  action A1 "Do it"           a rounded box; alias: task
  decision D1                 a branch; guards go on the arrows
  merge M1                    the branches coming back together
  fork F1                     one flow splitting into several
  join J1                     several coming back into one
  object O1 "Invoice"         a value passing along the flow
  final E1                    the bullseye it ends at; alias: end
  flow-final X1               this one branch stops here

Flows
  A -> B                      control flow
  D1 [yes] -> B               a guard on the branch
  A -.-> O1                   object flow (dashed)
  A -> B -> C                 chain

RULES
- The file is one `activity "Title" { ... }` block.
- Partitions are `lane L "Name" { ... }` and are drawn as columns, left to right in the order written.
- Declare every node inside the partition it belongs to, then wire them after or inside.
- A guard belongs on the arrow out of a decision: `D1 [yes] -> A2`.
- A decision has one flow in and several out; a merge has several in and one out.

WORKED EXAMPLE
activity "Client Visit" {
  lane SALES "Sales Person" {
    initial S1
    action A1 "Call client and set up appointment"
    decision D1
    action A4 "Send follow-up letter"
    decision D2
    final E1
  }

  lane CONS "Consultant" {
    action A2 "Prepare a laptop"
    action A3 "Meet with the client"
    action A5 "Create proposal"
    action A6 "Send proposal to client"
  }

  lane TECH "Corporate Technician" {
    action A7 "Prepare a conference room"
  }

  S1 -> A1 -> D1
  D1 [appointment offsite] -> A2
  D1 [appointment onsite] -> A7
  A2 -> A3
  A7 -> A3
  A3 -> A4 -> D2
  D2 [statement of problem] -> A5 -> A6 -> E1
  D2 [no statement of problem] -> E1
}

erd.name: entity relationship diagram
erd.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  erd "Title" {               open an entity relationship diagram
  entity E "table" {          an entity, with its attributes inside
  weak E "table" {            one that needs its owner to be told apart

Attributes
  "name" "type"               one attribute row
  pk "id" "bigint"            primary key
  fk "owner_id" "bigint"      foreign key; pfk for both
  "email" "varchar" unique    unique
  "closed_at" "date" null     may be missing; drawn as type?

Relations
  A -> B                      one to many, the usual case
  A one -> many B             the crow's foot at each end
  A many -> one B "label"     and what the relation is called
  A -.-> B                    non-identifying (dashed)
  ends                        one, many, one-or-many, zero-or-one

Which columns it joins
  A.id -> B.a_id              leaves that key and meets that one
  left out                    the keys are paired up on their names
  panel                       or set it in Tables, beside the relation

RULES
- The file is one `erd "Title" { ... }` block.
- An entity is `entity ID "table" { ... }`, and every attribute inside it is written in quotes.
- An attribute is `"name" "type"`, optionally opened with `pk`, `fk` or `pfk` and closed with `unique` or `null`.
- A relation is `A one -> many B`; leaving both ends out means one to many.
- The ends are `one`, `many`, `one-or-many` and `zero-or-one`. A dashed arrow is non-identifying.
- Either end may name the column it joins: `PASSENGER.id one -> many BOOKING.passenger_id`. Left out, the primary key is paired with the foreign key named after it.

WORKED EXAMPLE
erd "Airline Booking" {
  entity PASSENGER "passengers" {
    pk "id" "bigint"
    "first_name" "varchar(50)"
    "last_name" "varchar(50)"
    "passport_number" "varchar(20)" unique
    "country_of_residence" "varchar(50)" null
  }

  entity BOOKING "booking" {
    pk "booking_id" "bigint"
    fk "passenger_id" "bigint"
    fk "flight_id" "bigint"
    "status" "varchar(20)"
    "booking_platform" "varchar(20)"
  }

  entity FLIGHT "flights" {
    pk "flight_id" "bigint"
    fk "airline_id" "bigint"
    "departing_gate" "varchar(20)"
    "arriving_gate" "varchar(20)"
  }

  entity AIRLINE "airline" {
    pk "airline_id" "bigint"
    "airline_name" "varchar(50)"
    "country" "varchar(50)"
  }

  weak BAGGAGE "baggage" {
    pk "id" "bigint"
    fk "booking_id" "bigint"
    "weight_in_kg" "decimal(4,2)"
  }

  PASSENGER one -> many BOOKING "makes"
  AIRLINE one -> many FLIGHT "operates"
  FLIGHT one -> many BOOKING "carries"
  BOOKING one -.-> many BAGGAGE "checks in"
}

sequence.name: UML sequence diagram
sequence.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  sequence "Title" {          open a sequence diagram

Participants
  object B ":Order"           a named box over a lifeline
  actor A "Customer"          a stick figure
  boundary S "Screen"         what the outside world touches
  control C "Handler"         what runs the work
  entity E "Account"          what is stored
  database D "Ledger"         a store drawn as a drum

Messages
  A -> B "call()"             a call; opens an execution on B
  A ->> B "signal()"          asynchronous, open head
  B --> A "answer"            a reply; ends B's execution
  create A -> B "new"         B's lifeline starts here
  destroy A -> B "close"      B's lifeline ends with a cross
  B -> B "check()"            a call to itself, drawn as a loop

Fragments
  alt "guard" { … }           one section runs
  } else "guard" { … }        the next section of an alt
  opt "guard" { … }           runs only if the guard holds
  loop "while" { … }          runs again and again
  par { … } and { … }         the sections run alongside
  break / critical            the other two operators

Settings
  numbers on                  number every message in order
  activations off             leave the execution bars off
  style tinted                formal, tinted or bold
  colors colorful             or one colour: colors "#2a78d6"
  spacing 150                 least room between two lifelines
  step 46                     from one message down to the next
  text 12                     caption size
  size 700 420                how big it is drawn

RULES
- The file is one `sequence "Title" { ... }` block.
- Declare every participant before the messages, at the top level: `object B ":Order"`.
- Messages are written in the order they are sent, one per line, and that order is the diagram.
- `->` is a call, `->>` is asynchronous, `-->` is a reply. `create` and `destroy` open a message line.
- A fragment is a block: `alt "guard" { ... } else "guard" { ... }`. They may be nested.
- The execution bars are worked out from the messages; never try to place them.

WORKED EXAMPLE
sequence "Shopping Cart" {
  actor CUST "Customer"
  object CART ":Shopping Cart"
  object ORDER ":Order"
  object ITEM ":Item"

  numbers on
  activations on

  CUST -> CART "«create»"
  CART -> ORDER "getTotal()"
  ORDER -> ITEM "getPrice()"
  ITEM --> ORDER "itemPrice"
  ORDER -> ORDER "calculateTotal()"
  ORDER --> CART "totalPrice"
}

bar.name: bar chart
bar.briefing:
SYNTAX
Chart
  bar "Title" {               open a bar chart; close it with }

Readings
  Apples 40                   one bar, named and measured
  "Two words" 40              a name with a space goes in quotes
  categories A B C            name the bars, for grouped series
  series "Round 1" 10 20 12   one series across those categories
  series "R1" "#e34948" 10 20  a series in a colour of its own

Bars
  bars horizontal             vertical or horizontal
  layout stacked              grouped or stacked, for several series

Axes
  x "Caption"                 caption under the across axis
  y "Caption"                 caption beside the up axis
  grid value                  none, value, category, both
  range 0 250                 pin where the value axis runs

Look
  colors colorful             auto, single, colorful, warm, cool, ink
  colors "#2a78d6"            one colour, pinned
  style framed                plain, ruled, framed, bold
  legend bottom               auto, none, right, bottom, top
  values on                   write the number on every mark
  size 520 340                how big the chart is drawn
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `bar "Title" { ... }` block. Nothing may sit outside it.
- A reading is `Name 40`, one per line, and draws a bar per reading. A name with a space or a comma in it goes in quotes.
- Settings are written as `name value`, in any order, before or after the readings.
- A word that is a setting name is never read as a reading; quote it if you need it as a name.
- Use `series` only when there is more than one thing being measured; a single series needs no `series` line at all.
- Do not invent settings. Every one the language has is listed above.

WORKED EXAMPLE
bar "Favourite Fruit" {
  x "Favourite fruit"
  y "Number of students"

  Apples 9
  Bananas 16
  Oranges 10
  Grapes 7
}

line.name: line chart
line.briefing:
SYNTAX
Chart
  line "Title" {              open a line chart

Readings
  2017 8                      one reading, named and measured
  categories 2017 2018        name the readings along the axis
  series "Bears" 8 55 92      one line across those categories
  series "B" "#2a78d6" 8 55   a line in a colour of its own

Line
  markers on                  a dot at every reading
  curve on                    join the readings with a curve
  area on                     wash the space under the line

Axes
  x "Caption"                 caption under the across axis
  y "Caption"                 caption beside the up axis
  grid value                  none, value, category, both
  range 0 250                 pin where the value axis runs

Look
  colors colorful             auto, single, colorful, warm, cool, ink
  colors "#2a78d6"            one colour, pinned
  style framed                plain, ruled, framed, bold
  legend bottom               auto, none, right, bottom, top
  values on                   write the number on every mark
  size 520 340                how big the chart is drawn
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `line "Title" { ... }` block. Nothing may sit outside it.
- A reading is `Name 40`, one per line, and draws a line through the readings. A name with a space or a comma in it goes in quotes.
- Settings are written as `name value`, in any order, before or after the readings.
- A word that is a setting name is never read as a reading; quote it if you need it as a name.
- Use `series` only when there is more than one thing being measured; a single series needs no `series` line at all.
- Do not invent settings. Every one the language has is listed above.

WORKED EXAMPLE
line "Wildlife Population" {
  y "Animals counted"
  legend bottom

  categories 2017 2018 2019 2020 2021 2022
  series "Bears" 8 55 92 116 137 184
  series "Dolphins" 150 77 34 12 5 2
  series "Whales" 80 54 100 76 93 72
}

pie.name: pie chart
pie.briefing:
SYNTAX
Chart
  pie "Title" {               open a pie chart

Slices
  Apples 40                   one slice, named and measured
  "Mocha Marvels" 32.9        a name with a space goes in quotes
  series "Share" 40 60        the same slices, written as a series

Pie
  percent on                  read the values as shares of the whole
  donut 0.5                   open a hole in the middle, 0 to 0.9

Look
  colors colorful             auto, single, colorful, warm, cool, ink
  colors "#2a78d6"            one colour, pinned
  style framed                plain, ruled, framed, bold
  legend bottom               auto, none, right, bottom, top
  values on                   write the number on every mark
  size 520 340                how big the chart is drawn
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `pie "Title" { ... }` block. Nothing may sit outside it.
- A reading is `Name 40`, one per line, and draws a slice per reading. A name with a space or a comma in it goes in quotes.
- Settings are written as `name value`, in any order, before or after the readings.
- A word that is a setting name is never read as a reading; quote it if you need it as a name.
- Use `series` only when there is more than one thing being measured; a single series needs no `series` line at all.
- Do not invent settings. Every one the language has is listed above.

WORKED EXAMPLE
pie "Cookie Market Share, 2023" {
  percent on

  "Mocha Marvels" 32.9
  "Caramel Swirls" 24.4
  "PB Bliss" 19.0
  "Choco Chippers" 9.0
  "Mint Melts" 7.4
  "Berry Bursts" 7.2

scatter.name: scatter plot
scatter.briefing:
SYNTAX
Chart
  scatter "Title" {           open a scatter plot

Points
  (12, 40)                    one point, across then up
  (12, 40) "A. Cabbell"       a point with a name beside it
  series "Japan" (13, 4)      a named cloud of points
  series "J" "#e34948" (13, 4)  a cloud in a colour of its own

Cloud
  trend on                    one straight line of best fit
  markers on                  draw the points themselves

Axes
  x "Caption"                 caption under the across axis
  y "Caption"                 caption beside the up axis
  grid value                  none, value, category, both
  range 0 250                 pin where the value axis runs

Look
  colors colorful             auto, single, colorful, warm, cool, ink
  colors "#2a78d6"            one colour, pinned
  style framed                plain, ruled, framed, bold
  legend bottom               auto, none, right, bottom, top
  values on                   write the number on every mark
  size 520 340                how big the chart is drawn
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `scatter "Title" { ... }` block. Nothing may sit outside it.
- A reading is `Name 40`, one per line, and draws a point per reading. A name with a space or a comma in it goes in quotes.
- Settings are written as `name value`, in any order, before or after the readings.
- A word that is a setting name is never read as a reading; quote it if you need it as a name.
- Use `series` only when there is more than one thing being measured; a single series needs no `series` line at all.
- Do not invent settings. Every one the language has is listed above.

WORKED EXAMPLE
scatter "Local Index by Year" {
  x "Year"
  y "Local index"
  trend on

  series "Local index"
    (1900, 10) (1901, 9) (1902, 12) (1903, 15) (1904, 9) (1905, 40)
    (1906, 4) (1907, 19) (1908, 25) (1909, 14) (1910, 20) (1911, 38)
    (1912, 30) (1913, 60) (1914, 75) (1915, 55) (1916, 89) (1917, 95)
    (1918, 69) (1919, 100) (1920, 92)
}

mind.name: mind map
mind.briefing:
SYNTAX
Map
  mind "Central idea" {       open a mind map; the title is the middle

Branches
  "A branch"                  one branch off the idea
  "A branch" {                a branch with more hanging off it
  "A branch" "#2a78d6"        a branch in a colour of its own
  "A branch" circle           a branch drawn as a different shape

Arrangement
  layout radial               radial, sides, down
  spread 150                  how far a level sits from the one above
  line curve                  curve, elbow, straight
  shape round                 round, pill, box, circle, diamond, hex, none

Look
  colors colorful             auto, single, colorful, warm, cool, ink
  branch on                   one hue per branch, rather than per level
  style formal                formal, soft, bold, wire
  text 13                     how big a caption is set
  size 760 560                how big the map is drawn
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `mind "Title" { ... }` block. Nothing may sit outside it.
- The title is the idea in the middle; everything else hangs off it.
- A branch is a caption in quotes on its own line. Give it a `{ ... }` block for whatever hangs off it, nested as deep as you like.
- A colour and a shape may follow a branch's caption, in that order, and apply to that branch alone.
- Settings are written as `name value`, in any order.
- Do not invent settings. Every one the language has is listed above.

WORKED EXAMPLE
mind "Web Design" {
  "Visual Design" {
    "Colour Scheme"
    "Typography"
    "Imagery and Icons"
  }
  "User Experience" {
    "Wireframing"
    "User Research"
    "Usability Testing"
  }
  "Development" {
    "Responsive Design"
    "JavaScript"
    "HTML and CSS"
  }
  "Content Strategy" {
    "Copywriting"
    "Search Engine Optimisation"
    "Content Management"
  }
}

matrix.name: matrix table
matrix.briefing:
SYNTAX
Matrix
  matrix "Title" {            open a matrix table

Columns
  corner "Name / Skill"       caption in the top-left corner
  column "Safety"             one column heading
  column "3-GEN" "Kaizen"     a column under a spanning group heading
  column "Safety" "" "#2a78d6"  a heading with its own fill

Rows and cells
  row "Amir" "x" "" "Trainer"  one value per column; any text is valid
  row "Budi" {                open a row when cells need their own colours
  cell "High" "#00a86b"       one cell value and an optional fill
  color "#fff2cc"             the row heading's own fill, inside a row block

Arrangement
  header vertical             horizontal or vertical column labels
  align center                left, center, right
  row-header 140              width of the headings down the left
  header-height 112           height of the column labels

Look
  style headers               plain, headers, banded, heatmap
  header-color "#2a78d6"      shared column-heading colour
  row-color "#dce9f8"         shared row-heading colour
  cell-color "#fff2cc"        body fill for bands or a heatmap
  grid-color "#1f2933"        lines and the title
  border 1.5                  grid-line weight
  text 13                     caption size
  size 760 460                how big the matrix is drawn
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `matrix "Title" { ... }` block. Nothing may sit outside it.
- Declare columns first with `column "Name"`; an optional second caption groups consecutive columns under one spanning heading.
- A compact row is `row "Name" "cell 1" "cell 2"`. It must not have more values than there are columns; omitted values are empty.
- When cells need colours, open a row block and write each as `cell "anything" "#rrggbb"`. The colour is optional and the value remains text.
- A row block may also contain `color "#rrggbb"` for the heading down the left.
- Settings are written as `name value`, in any order.
- Do not invent settings. Every one the language has is listed above.

WORKED EXAMPLE
matrix "Team skill matrix" {
  corner "Name / Skill"

  column "3-GEN" "GENBA KAIZEN"

venn.name: Venn diagram
venn.briefing:
SYNTAX
Diagram
  venn "Title" {              open a Venn diagram

Sets
  set A "Human"               name a ring; two or three of them
  set A "Human" "#2a78d6"     a ring in a colour of its own
  overlap 0.5                 how far the rings sit into each other

Regions
  A "126"                     what is only in A
  AB "32"                     what is in A and B but not C
  ABC "9"                     what is in all three
  out "Kermit"                what is in none of them

Look
  style tint                  outline, tint, bold
  colors colorful             auto, single, colorful, warm, cool, ink
  zeros on                    write a nought in an empty region
  size 520 460                how big the diagram is drawn
  # comment                   line comment (also //)

RULES
- The file is one `venn "Title" { ... }` block. Nothing may sit outside it.
- Declare two or three sets with `set A "Name"`, in order: A, then B, then C.
- A region is named by the sets it belongs to — `A`, `AB`, `ABC` — and `out` is what belongs to none of them.
- A region nobody names is left empty rather than drawn as a blank.
- Settings are written as `name value`, in any order.
- Do not invent settings. Every one the language has is listed above.

WORKED EXAMPLE
venn "Three sets" {
  set A "Set 1"
  set B "Set 2"
  set C "Set 3"

  A "126"
  B "129"
  C "128"
  AB "32"
  AC "33"
  BC "30"
  ABC "9"
}
